local_checks.invariant: Every /admin route in adm_bp (29 routes) requires a revalidated admin session (sid not revoked + credential fingerprint of ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH/TOTP reference) before any read or state change

Bulk operations (avisos, cobranca em lote) and destructive ones (remover aluno) also require an additional session-bound token. No unguarded route found; session['tipo_usuario']='admin' is set only in usuario_bp._abrir_sessao_admin.

local_checks.invariant: Admin-only routes in turma/academia/planilha/OAuth/pix-sync blueprints use admin_requerido or sessao_administrativa_valida; professor routes bind turma.professor_id to the revalidated professor
local_checks.result: All /admin/* routes in these blueprints carry @admin_requerido (or explicit sessao_administrativa_valida in pix_bp sincronizar). /turmas/<id> and /turmas/<id>/presenca apply professor_ou_admin_requerido plus _acesso_permitido (turma.professor_id == professor.id); matricular/desmatricular are admin-only; presence writes are limited to enrolled students of that turma. /professores/<id>/foto exposes unpublished photo only to admin or the professor himself.

local_checks.invariant: Cookie-authenticated mutations are covered by CSRF protection; no state-changing GET
local_checks.result: CSRFProtect is initialized globally (servidor.py:183); the only exemption is the HMAC-signed MP webhook (pix_bp.py:479). Admin/professor mutations are POST. The GET /admin/*/conectar routes only write OAuth state into the caller's own session (OAuth callback binding is peer-owned).

local_checks.invariant: Lower-trust principals (aluno, professor of another turma) cannot reach admin routes or another professor's turma
local_checks.result: Sandboxed pytest with dummy records: aluno on /admin and /admin/planilha -> 302 /login; professor prof1 on turma of prof2 -> GET 403, POST presenca 403; professor on /turmas/<id>/matricular -> 302 /login; professor on /admin -> 302 /login.

hardening_notes: blueprints/usuario_bp.py:685 checks login uniqueness only against Aluno, not Professor/ADMIN_USER; login order is admin->professor->aluno, so a student renaming to a professor's login only shadows themself (no cross-principal effect found), but a global uniqueness check would remove the ambiguity.

blueprints/adm_bp.py uses an explicit per-handler `if not usuario_e_admin()` rather than a blueprint-level before_request; all 29 current routes have it, but a before_request guard on admin_bp would fail closed for future routes.

local_checks.invariant: Google login callback accepts only the state issued to this session (one-time, 10-minute TTL), exchanges the code with the session's PKCE verifier and client secret, uses a fixed redirect_uri from APP_BASE_URL, requires email_verified is True, and rotates the session on success
local_checks.result: Holds. The state is popped from the session before validation and compared with hmac.compare_digest after type and TTL checks (google_login.py:43-53, 97-101). The code is exchanged with code_verifier, client_secret and a redirect_uri that does not depend on the Host header (106-114). No ID token is consumed; identity comes from userinfo, called with the access token this server just obtained. email_verified must be exactly True (128). acesso_ativado, status and ativo are checked, then session.clear() + iniciar_sessao() + registrar_credencial run (151-174). Marking email_verificado on pending accounts (141-144) belongs to the peer account-linking unit and was not judged here.

local_checks.invariant: MP OAuth callback is admin-only, bound to a one-time session state with TTL plus a PKCE S256 verifier, and stores tokens encrypted
local_checks.result: Holds. conectar/callback are @admin_requerido. The state and verifier are generated with secrets (mercado_pago_conta.py:160-164) and popped once in the callback (mercado_pago_oauth_bp.py:109). The provider's error param is handled before the state check, but that path only shows a flash message and changes no state. The code length is capped and _autorizacao_valida compares in constant time with a TTL. The token exchange sends the verifier and the fixed redirect_uri. Tokens are Fernet-encrypted (authenticated) with MERCADO_PAGO_TOKEN_KEY or an HKDF-derived subkey of SECRET_KEY (info-separated). A decrypt failure raises ConexaoIlegivel/MercadoPagoIndisponivel and never falls back to plaintext. access_token_vigente falls back to the env token only when no connection row exists.

local_checks.invariant: Gmail OAuth callback is admin-only and bound to a one-time session state with TTL; the refresh token is stored with authenticated encryption and never used if decryption fails
local_checks.result: Holds. Both routes are @admin_requerido. The state is popped and compared with hmac.compare_digest under a 600 s TTL (gmail_oauth_bp.py:34-41). The redirect_uri comes from APP_BASE_URL. The refresh token is Fernet-encrypted with an HKDF(SECRET_KEY, info='extremeteam/gmail/tokens/v1') key, and _decifrar raises on InvalidToken. PKCE is absent (see hardening). With session-bound state and an admin-only callback, an injected code needs the admin's own session, so there is no cross-principal impact.

hardening_notes: Gmail OAuth (servicos/gmail_conta.py nova_autorizacao/trocar_codigo) sends no PKCE, unlike the Google login and Mercado Pago flows. The state is session-bound and the callback is admin-only, so no cross-principal impact was found; adding S256 PKCE would make the three flows consistent.

The admin TOTP reuse block fails open when limiter storage (Redis) errors (blueprints/usuario_bp.py:226-238). This is a deliberate availability trade-off: password and code are still required, and only replay protection within about 90 s is lost.

The admin TOTP pending marker (admin_segundo_fator) stores only a timestamp, not the credential reference that passed the password step. A password rotation within the 5-minute window does not void the pending step; the TOTP code is still required.

Investigation note: in the test suite, the contexto_app fixture keeps an outer app context, so flask.g is shared across test-client requests and _sessao_ativa's g._sessao_conferida cache can mask revocation. Revocation tests should not hold an app context across requests.

local_checks.result: 4 tests passed: approval carrying another mensalidade's reference left target 'pendente'; amount 1.00 vs 150.00 left 'pendente'; approval without external_reference left 'pendente'; after approval by id 333, later rejected(334)/in_process(335)/refunded(336) kept 'pago' with provider_payment_id 333; refund of 333 -> 'reembolsado'; a stale approved(333) afterwards kept 'reembolsado'.

local_checks.invariant: State machine and concurrency: Pix/checkout creation is owner-or-admin, only for payable states, under row lock, and replaced charges cannot settle a different amount; checkout return/status polling ignore URL parameters
local_checks.result: criar_pix/abrir_checkout lock the row (bloquear_para_atualizacao) and re-check status/provider id after the MP call; _acesso_permitido revalidates the session in DB; retorno_checkout uses only the stored checkout_external_reference. hardening_notes: Promotional price lock-in: _nova_cobranca stores preco(plano, hoje) and unpaid charges never expire or reprice. abrir_vigencia reopens the period on late payment, so a student can create a charge during a promotion and pay the promotional price at any later date (dao/financeiroDAO.py:287-309, 636-662). This is documented as intended. If policy requires it, reprice or expire unpaid charges after the promotion ends.

Refund/chargeback (marcar_reembolsado_via_webhook, dao/financeiroDAO.py:943-952) revokes vigencia but leaves the Matricula auto-created by efetivar_turma_da_cobranca. Each paid charge can add another turma, and enrollments are never removed. A charged-back student keeps a seat in a capacity-limited turma until an admin intervenes.

Interactive status polling, checkout return and admin sync call _processar_status_mp without bloquear_para_atualizacao (blueprints/pix_bp.py:354-383, checkout_bp.py:221-232, pix_bp.py:408-428). A refund webhook committed while a poller holds an older 'approved' API result could be overwritten back to 'pago'. The window is only the length of one API call (about 3 s) and is not attacker-driven. Locking the row before applying the result would close it.

_primeira_entrega_webhook fails open when the limiter storage errors (blueprints/pix_bp.py:463-467). This is acceptable only because processing is idempotent and always re-fetches the payment from the API.

A replan after the checkout preference expires (60 min) can leave a boleto/pending payment already issued at the old amount. If paid, it is refused by the amount check and logged only, so the student's money arrives without settlement and an admin must reconcile it (dao/financeiroDAO.py:273-280 does not consider checkout-originated pending payments).

local_checks.invariant: Recovery token is CSPRNG, stored only as SHA-256, bound to the CPF+email-matched account with acesso_ativado, expires in 30 min, is single-use, supersedes earlier tokens, and its link origin comes from configuration rather than the Host header
local_checks.result: secrets.token_urlsafe(32) (usuario_bp.py:979), only the sha256 is stored (986), expiry is 30 min (987, 961) and is checked with <= (1019). The token is looked up by an exact indexed hash, with no timing-sensitive compare on the secret. On success _revogar_tokens_de_conta clears the recovery, invite and email-change tokens (1031, 635-648). One column per account means a new request overwrites the earlier hash. url_publica uses APP_BASE_URL only (servicos/urls.py:11-34), not Host. The token email bypasses the cleartext emails_pendentes queue (_enviar_em_segundo_plano, 129-135, 990). Both routes are rate limited (963-968, 1007-1011). The response is identical for unknown and known CPF+email (998).

local_checks.invariant: A password reset invalidates existing sessions and pending account-redirect tokens
local_checks.result: set_senha changes senha_hash, and aluno_autorizado revalidates the credential fingerprint on every request (autorizacao.py:121-137), so sessions opened before the reset die. Pending email-change and invite tokens are cleared. Existing regression tests cover session revocation and expiry (tests/test_regressao_auditoria.py:138,165,467).

local_checks.invariant: Bounded local check: a superseded token is rejected, the latest token works once, and reuse is rejected
local_checks.result: Sandboxed pytest: the old token after a new request gave 'Link inválido' (True), the new token was accepted ('Senha alterada', True), and reusing it was rejected ('Link inválido', True).

local_checks.invariant: An invite token cannot be replayed into an already-activated account, and two concurrent activations cannot overwrite each other's credentials
local_checks.result: aluno_do_token refuses activated accounts (convites.py:62-63). ativar_acesso writes conditionally (usuario_bp.py:926-933) on the token hash, expiry, senha_hash IS NULL and unchanged email, so it is atomic. The token is delivered only to the admin-registered aluno.email (convites.py:76-90).

hardening_notes: The /cadastrar verification link (usuario_bp.py:420-431) goes through fila_email.enfileirar_transacional, so the token is stored in cleartext in emails_pendentes.link_url. The design comment at usuario_bp.py:129-135 says token emails must avoid the queue (peer-owned fila_email unit).

confirmar_email (usuario_bp.py:849) does not recheck that email_pendente is still unused. If another account claimed that address meanwhile, the unique constraint raises an IntegrityError (500) rather than a clean refusal. This is not a security bypass, because the DB constraint holds.

Signup collision checks and email-change uniqueness consider only Aluno.email, not other accounts' email_pendente. Two accounts can hold the same pending address, and the first to confirm wins. There is no cross-account impact, because confirmation needs the token sent to that address.
